learningObjectives.title: Flashpoints outside Europe (Korea, Cuba, Vietnam, Afghanistan)
The end of the Cold War 1985-91

questions.q: Which three leaders attended the Yalta Conference in February 1945?
options: Roosevelt, Churchill and Stalin
Truman, Attlee and Stalin
Truman, Churchill and Khrushchev
Roosevelt, Attlee and Stalin
questions.explain: Yalta in February 1945 brought together the American, British and Soviet leaders Roosevelt, Churchill and Stalin.

questions.q: In his 1946 Fulton speech, what did Churchill mean by the 'Iron Curtain'?
options: The growing division between the communist East and the capitalist West of Europe
A physical wall built across the centre of Berlin
The Soviet blockade of all sea routes to Britain
The wartime alliance between the USA and USSR
questions.explain: Churchill used the phrase to describe how Soviet control was cutting communist Eastern Europe off from the West.

questions.q: What was the main aim of the Truman Doctrine (1947)?
options: To contain the spread of communism by supporting countries threatened by it
To provide economic aid only to communist states
To disarm the United States after the war
To form a military alliance with the Soviet Union
questions.explain: The Truman Doctrine committed the USA to containment, helping nations resisting communist takeover.

questions.q: What was the Marshall Plan (1947)?
options: American economic aid to help rebuild the countries of Europe
A Soviet plan to blockade West Berlin
A military alliance of Western European states
A plan to divide Germany into four zones
questions.explain: The Marshall Plan offered US financial aid to rebuild European economies and resist communism.

questions.q: Why was NATO set up in 1949?
options: To provide a defensive military alliance for Western nations against the Soviet threat
To give economic aid to Eastern Europe
To govern the city of Berlin jointly
To unite Germany under one government
questions.explain: NATO was a collective-defence alliance of the USA and Western states formed to deter Soviet aggression.

questions.q: A 1945 cartoon shows Truman and Stalin glaring at one another across a table at Potsdam. Which factor best explains the tension shown?
options: Disagreements over the future of Germany and Eastern Europe
A dispute over Marshall Aid, which had not yet been created
The building of the Berlin Wall
The Soviet invasion of Afghanistan
questions.explain: At Potsdam, disputes over reparations, Germany and Soviet control of Eastern Europe deepened distrust.

questions.q: In which year did the Berlin Blockade begin?
questions.explain: Stalin blockaded West Berlin's land routes from June 1948 until May 1949.

questions.q: How did the Western powers respond to the Berlin Blockade?
options: They flew supplies into West Berlin in a massive airlift
They launched a military invasion of East Germany
They abandoned West Berlin to the Soviets
They immediately built the Berlin Wall
questions.explain: The Berlin Airlift supplied West Berlin by air for almost a year until Stalin lifted the blockade.

questions.q: In which year was the Berlin Wall built?
questions.explain: The East German government began building the Berlin Wall in August 1961.

questions.q: In 1956 the Hungarian leader Imre Nagy announced that Hungary would leave the Warsaw Pact. What was the Soviet response?
options: Soviet tanks and troops invaded to crush the uprising
The USSR allowed Hungary to become neutral
The USA sent troops to defend Hungary
The United Nations took control of Hungary
questions.explain: The USSR sent in the Red Army in November 1956, crushing the rising and later executing Nagy.

questions.q: How were Dubcek's reforms during the 1968 Prague Spring often described?
options: 'Socialism with a human face'
'Peaceful coexistence'
'The domino theory'
'Mutually assured destruction'
questions.explain: Dubcek's liberalising reforms in Czechoslovakia were known as creating 'socialism with a human face'.

questions.q: The Korean War began in 1950 when North Korea crossed which dividing line to invade the South?
options: The 38th parallel
The Iron Curtain
The Berlin Wall
The 17th parallel
questions.explain: North Korean forces crossed the 38th parallel in June 1950, beginning the Korean War.

questions.q: What was the Bay of Pigs incident of 1961?
options: A failed US-backed invasion of Cuba by anti-Castro exiles
A Soviet nuclear test carried out in Cuba
The building of missile bases across Cuba
A naval blockade of Cuba by the USA
questions.explain: The CIA-backed invasion by Cuban exiles failed, embarrassing the USA and pushing Castro towards the USSR.

questions.q: In which year did the Cuban Missile Crisis take place?
questions.explain: The Cuban Missile Crisis unfolded in October 1962.

questions.q: The Cuban Missile Crisis was resolved when Khrushchev agreed to remove Soviet missiles from Cuba. What did the USA agree to do in return?
options: Promise not to invade Cuba and secretly remove its missiles from Turkey
Give large-scale economic aid to the Soviet Union
Remove all its troops from Western Europe
Hand West Berlin over to the USSR
questions.explain: The USA publicly pledged not to invade Cuba and secretly agreed to withdraw its missiles from Turkey.

questions.q: In which year did the Soviet Union invade Afghanistan?
questions.explain: Soviet forces invaded Afghanistan in December 1979.

questions.q: Who became leader of the Soviet Union in 1985?
options: Mikhail Gorbachev
Leonid Brezhnev
Nikita Khrushchev
Boris Yeltsin
questions.explain: Gorbachev became Soviet leader in 1985 and introduced far-reaching reforms.

questions.q: What did Gorbachev's policies of glasnost and perestroika mean?
options: 'Openness' and 'restructuring' of Soviet society and the economy
'Containment' and 'deterrence' of the West
'Censorship' and 'central planning'
'Isolation' and 'rearmament'
questions.explain: Glasnost meant greater openness while perestroika meant economic and political restructuring.

questions.q: Why was the fall of the Berlin Wall in 1989 so significant?
options: It symbolised the collapse of communist control in Eastern Europe
It marked the start of the Berlin Blockade
It triggered the Cuban Missile Crisis
It led to the creation of NATO
questions.explain: The wall's fall in November 1989 came to symbolise the end of communist rule across Eastern Europe.

questions.q: By December 1991 the USSR had broken apart into separate independent states. Which development best explains this collapse?
options: Gorbachev's reforms weakened Communist Party control and encouraged nationalist independence movements
The Marshall Plan bankrupted the Soviet economy
NATO forces invaded the Soviet Union
The Berlin Blockade cut off Moscow's supplies
questions.explain: Gorbachev's reforms loosened central control, allowing Soviet republics to break away and the USSR to dissolve in 1991.
